images.title: Add one column, add the rows
images.purpose: Shows the dot rectangle of the practice tool in its simplest state: 4 rows of 5 dots with one more column of 4 added past a divider, so 4 × 6 = 4 × 5 + 4 × 1.
images.composition: One small dot rectangle centred, split by one vertical dashed divider. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A dot array of exactly 4 rows. Left of the divider, 5 columns of teal (#0072B2) dots (20 dots). A vertical dashed reddish purple (#CC79A7) divider line runs top to bottom between the 5th and 6th columns. Right of the divider, 1 column of amber (#E69F00) dots (4 dots). All dots are the same size and evenly spaced. Under the teal part the label '4 × 5 = 20'; under the amber column the label '4 × 1 = 4'. Above the whole array, centred, the label '4 × 6 = 24'. Exactly 20 teal dots, 4 amber dots, 1 divider.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Splitting the columns splits the product: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
images.description: Shows the dot rectangle of the practice tool in its simplest state: 4 rows of 5 dots with one more column of 4 added past a divider, so 4 × 6 = 4 × 5 + 4 × 1.
images.context: Distributive area tool: a = 4, b = 5, c = 1.

image_decisions.why: The practice is about growing a product by parts; the simplest dot split shows the move the tool makes.
